notes: Japanese rows are machine translations (GPT-4.1-mini) with 94% automatic labels; the human-validated subset (rightmost Table 2 block, 51.76) is a smaller alternative not released as a separate file. || [normalize 2026-09-07] test.csv verified (12,780 rows; Utterance, Response, validate_or_not, confidence, language; 8,144 x 0 / 4,636 x 1). Gold remapped 1 -> validate, 0 -> non-validate; 'non-validate' is listed first so that a 'non-validate' reply is not read as 'validate' (the runner's word-boundary match would otherwise hit both). A reply with neither label counts as a miss (the paper's 'no match = non-validate' default is not applied by the runner). || [triage 2026-09-09 g1] DEVIATION. Cell confirmed (Table 2, Multilingual block, M-EDESConv Overall M-F1 51.68; target-class P/R/F1 41.43/79.25/54.41). Replies are bare labels: validate 10,645, non-validate 2,051, 77 'Please provide the utterances you'd like me to classify.' (unparsed) per seed. Our validate-class P/R/F1 38.3/88.0/53.4 reproduces the paper's F1, but the model now answers validate for 83% of utterances (about 69% implied by the paper's P/R), which halves the non-validate F1 (29.7 vs about 49) -> macro 41.5 (per seed 41.5/41.4/41.7). Per language (seed 0): en 44.3 (paper English block 55.36), ja 37.5 (paper 47.03). Applying the config's 'no match = non-validate' default gives 42.0. Snapshot pinned (9 fingerprints); most plausibly prompt placement / separator sensitivity (the utterance is appended after the instruction without a marker; 77 replies ask for the utterances). No fix possible offline.
